issues.reason: 'was up 5.91 points' is the very shape the Measure rule specifies — 'scale = the surface dimension: the gradable adjective if one is stated', exactly as 'Alice is 6 feet tall' → (Measure alice tall 6 foot) — so (Measure ... up 5.91 point) records what the sentence says and nothing false; that a delta has no dedicated carrier is the coverage gap the reviewer also files.

The instruction set already derives an unstated dimension name from the clause ('costs $20' → price), and (Measure ... level 1674.35 point) is true of 'at 1,674.35' and well-typed (a scale symbol, not a coined head), so this is licensed improvisation in gap territory rather than a defect.

gaps_confirmed: delta / change-of-value measures ('was up 5.91 points'): Measure and MeasureAtLeast/AtMost record absolute values and MoreBy needs two named relata, so a bare rise or fall has no licensed carrier
appositional / equivalence 'or' restating one quantity in another unit ('5.91 points, or 0.35 percent'): the Disjunction section makes every 'or' an opaque (Or …), which is not this reading
a bare 'at <number>' value with no dimension noun and no unit in the text
discourse-initial 'But' whose contrasting clause lies outside the supplied TEXT: the adversative rule needs two reified endpoints
new_gaps: 'percent' as a Measure unit: the unit lexicon and canonical-unit conversion cover length / mass / time / temperature, so a ratio-valued magnitude has no dimension and no canonical form
notes: Both issues restate the reviewer's own gaps as defects; every atom is true of the sentence and structurally well-formed, and the Past wrappers on the measures follow the stated tense-wrapping rule.
